subject: Acme procurement & security next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>; Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Acme procurement & security next steps

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for the call today — good overview of Acme's use case and requirements. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we have clear ownership: 

Summary:
- Use case: internal knowledge retrieval + customer-facing summarization (mid-sized queries, ~10-30 tokens per request on average).
- Expected monthly usage: pilot ~50k tokens, piloting to prod ~2-3M tokens/month if successful.
- Security: SOC 2 compliance required, DPA is required, and procurement needs a completed security questionnaire.

Open actions / next steps:
1) Marissa (me) — share SOC 2 report and our standard DPA template (attached).
2) Samantha / Tom — confirm procurement path: will you process via PO (preferred) or corporate card for pilot? Also let us know if you prefer Marketplace (AWS Marketplace/GCP) purchasing or direct order form.
3) Tom — please attach any procurement-specific checklist or vendor setup form you want us to complete.
4) Acme — send over your security questionnaire (spreadsheet/PDF). Rishi our SE will fill the technical parts; legal (cc'd) will handle contract redlines.

Timing: if we get the questionnaire and confirm PO vs card this week, typical procurement+security turnaround for customers of your size is 1-3 weeks for pilot. Contract redlines usually take 3-7 business days once legal has everything.

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Report_2026.pdf (stub), Redwood_DPA_v3.1.pdf (stub)

I'll follow up with a short quote/term sheet once you confirm the path. Happy to jump on another call with procurement/legal if that helps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0172

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>

Cc: Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Acme procurement & security next steps

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few quick answers and questions from procurement/ops perspective:

- Procurement path: Acme prefers to use PO for any vendor engagement >$5k/month. For an initial pilot under $5k we can usually charge to a corporate card, but we'd prefer to move to PO for production.
- Marketplace: we're interested in AWS Marketplace if available because it simplifies billing and procurement approvals, but not required if PO is straightforward. Are you listed on AWS Marketplace?
- Timeline: sounds reasonable. If we can get SOC 2 and the DPA today, I'll route to procurement. I've attached our vendor onboarding checklist for your team to review.

Attaching: ACME_Vendor_Onboarding_Checklist.pdf (stub)

I'll loop Tom (procurement lead) to coordinate the PO/payment path and he can send the security questionnaire.

Samantha
Samantha Lee
Director, Vendor Operations | Acme Corp
samantha.lee@acme.com

From: Tom Bennett <tom.bennett@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>; Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@acme.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme procurement & security next steps

Hi Marissa / Samantha,

Thanks — copying my procurement checklist below and attaching the security questionnaire we use. Main items we need to complete vendor setup:

- Completed security questionnaire (attached)
- W9 and vendor onboarding form (we can send via Coupa if needed)
- Approved SOW or Master Services Agreement (MSA) and purchase order (we prefer Net30 payment terms on PO)
- Contact for billing and technical escalation

Marketplace note: we prefer AWS Marketplace for production purchases but would like to keep the pilot off-marketplace if possible to avoid the extra procurement steps; that said, if Redwood is already in Marketplace, it is a plus.

Attaching: ACME_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx (filled by Acme)

Can your legal team (or someone from Redwood) confirm whether Redwood accepts Net30 on PO and whether you can sign our standard MSA with minor redlines? If not, we can do a short-term order form for the pilot and proceed to full MSA later.

Tom Bennett
Procurement Lead | Acme Corp

Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Acme procurement & security next steps

Tom / Samantha — great, thanks for the checklist and the questionnaire. Answers inline and attachments included below.

Quick answers:
- PO vs card: PO is fine; we routinely accept PO with Net30 on production contracts. For pilots we can accept card to speed things up and convert to PO for production.
- Marketplace: Redwood is listed on AWS Marketplace (we can provide the listing ID). If you prefer to purchase via Marketplace for production, we can facilitate that — pilot can be direct.
- Contract redlines: our legal lead (cc'd: Dev Patel) can review your standard MSA and typically responds within 3-7 business days for minor redlines. Larger legal asks may take longer.

Attached for your review: Redwood_SOC2_Report_2026.pdf (stub), Redwood_DPA_v3.1.pdf (stub) — and I've uploaded a clean copy of the DPA to the DocuSign link below if you'd like an executed version for procurement.

Next proposed steps:
1) Acme to confirm pilot payment method (card vs PO). If card, we'll send a short order form; if PO, please send the PO once legal approves MSA/order form.
2) Samantha / Tom — please confirm the HubSpot deal contact and billing contact so we can populate vendor setup (I added the hubspot link below).
3) Rishi will review the security questionnaire and fill the technical sections; Dev will handle legal redlines.

Links: https://hubspot.company/deal/ACME-7895, DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/contract/ACME-7895

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_Report_2026.pdf, Redwood_DPA_v3.1.pdf

If you want, we can book a 30-min legal/procurement sync next week — Dev, Rishi, Tom, Samantha?

Thanks,
